questions.q: Why use the geometric mean for ratios to a baseline?
options: A 2x gain on one series and a 2x loss on another cancel to 1.0.

questions.q: Ratios to seasonal naive: 0.25 and 1.0. What is the geometric mean?
Which are valid reasons a zero-shot result may be too good? Select all.
options: The test data were in the pre-training corpus.
The benchmark is old and was used for tuning.
The context was longer than the data.
why: Yes, repeated use lets models fit the benchmark.
A longer context limit is not a reason for inflated scores.
MASE is a fair scale-free metric.

questions.q: A leaderboard post has no date or version. What do you do?
options: Treat the ranking as unverified and check the live leaderboard and its settings.
why: Leaderboards are useful when read with care.

questions.q: In your harness a series has history shorter than one season. What should happen?
options: Skip it for all models and report how many were skipped.
Drop it only for the model that fails.
why: Correct: the same rule for all models.

questions.q: Model B has a better geometric mean than model A, but loses badly on the 3 largest-revenue series. What do you do?
options: Report both, weigh by business value, and consider using different models for different segments.
Pick B because the geometric mean is better.
why: One aggregate can hide costly failures.
